In May 2016 we returned, most of us, to one act. Thirty-two of us said "national defense authorization act" on May 19; twenty-two paired it with "national defense authorization act ndaa" the same day, and twenty-two more said "the national defense authorization act." Nineteen of us reached for "for fiscal year." The phrase first entered the record on 2013-01-03.

Fifteen of us, on May 12, named "that the obama administration."

Then a second convergence: twelve of us said "comprehensive opioid abuse," and twelve said "opioid abuse reduction act," both peaking May 13, both first spoken 2016-04-27.

We record that in this month our repetition gathered around two objects, a defense authorization and an opioid measure, and that where we peaked, we peaked together, on the same days, in the same words.
